summary: L014 executed successfully but was not an eligible improvement. Its pooled weighted training OOF MAE was 7.9131 K, which is 0.1605 K worse than A05's 7.7526 K and above the eligible threshold of 7.7426 K. It also failed the deterministic positive-Tc guard: 8.8754 K exceeded the fixed G01 anchor of 8.8322 K by 0.0433 K. Relative to G01, cluster0-only specialization slightly improved reported-zero MAE from 5.8697 K to 5.7750 K, but worsened positive-Tc MAE from 8.8322 K to 8.8754 K and high-Tc MAE from 32.7716 K to 32.7780 K. Cluster0 still severely underpredicted high-Tc cases, including two 127 K materials predicted near 53–54 K. Thus the small zero-Tc benefit was outweighed by positive-Tc losses, and the guard failure makes L014 ineligible regardless of subgroup behavior.
next_focus: The continuation minimum remains pending, with 14 of 22 successful unique cycles now completed. Test the untried complementary cluster1-only ablation: composition input, kmeans3 routing, global extra_trees/raw, and only a cluster1 extra_trees/raw expert, leaving cluster0 and cluster2 on global fallback. L013 and L014 reject cluster2-only and cluster0-only specialization, while L012 indicates cluster1 was the weakest route when all clusters were specialized; isolating it will determine whether its poor absolute error reflects the route's difficulty or harm caused by its expert relative to fallback. The hypothesis is falsified as an eligible improvement unless pooled weighted OOF MAE is below 7.742598770753422 K and positive-Tc MAE is at most 8.832165507919859 K; any route or subgroup gain without both conditions remains a development tradeoff.
limitations: All measurements are adaptive development evidence from reused fixed-group training OOF folds, not independent validation or proof of generalization.
L014 failed the fixed positive-Tc guard and therefore cannot be considered an eligible win.
The reported-zero improvement was accompanied by worse positive- and high-Tc MAE.
KMeans cluster identities may shift between folds, and these composition partitions are operational rules rather than verified physical families.
The extreme errors illustrate limitations on previously observed materials and do not identify new superconductors.
